summary:
ARES is a student prototype for exploring Mars locations and planning rover routes. It brings together maps of Gale Crater / Mount Sharp, Jezero Crater, and Olympus Mons with points of interest and scientific context. Its FastAPI backend provides region and point-of-interest information and calculates great-circle distances between requested route coordinates.

The route planner is geometry-only. It does not check terrain, slope, elevation, hazards, or whether a route is traversable, so it must not be treated as a safety assessment or real navigation tool. ARES is designed to make Mars exploration information easier to explore and to show where better terrain data would be needed.
details:
ARES (Astronaut Route Exploration & Survival) is a student prototype for exploring Mars locations and planning rover routes. It provides interactive maps and scientific points of interest for Gale Crater / Mount Sharp, Jezero Crater, and Olympus Mons. The backend uses Python and FastAPI; the frontend uses Svelte, TypeScript, and Vite.

The route planner calculates great-circle distance between two coordinates. It does not check terrain, slope, elevation, hazards, or traversability, so it cannot determine whether a route is safe. The map’s colorized MOLA imagery is for visual context and is not used as numerical elevation data. ARES is an exploration and learning tool, not operational navigation software.
